description_full: Afya Limited operates as a medical education group in Brazil. The company operates in three segments: Undergraduate, Continuing Education, and Medical Practice Solutions. The Undergraduate segment offers educational services through undergraduate courses related to medical school, health sciences, and other non-health undergraduate programs, including medicine, dentistry, nursing, radiology, psychology, pharmacy, physical education, physiotherapy, nutrition, biomedicine, business administration, accounting, law, civil and industrial engineering, and pedagogy. The Continuing Education segment provides medical education, including residency preparation programs, specialization test preparation, graduate courses in medicine, and digital and in-person professional development for physicians and medical students. The Medical Practice Solutions segment offers clinical decision support platforms, medical practice management software, healthcare financial services, and digital healthcare ecosystem solutions, such as electronic medical records, practice management tools, telemedicine, digital prescriptions, and doctor-patient relationship platforms. This segment also provides a subscription-based mobile app and website portal that focuses on assisting health professionals and students with clinical decision-making through tools, such as medical calculators, charts, and updated content, as well as prescriptions, clinical scores, medical procedures and laboratory exams, and others. The company also offers educational health and medical imaging; and other programs to lifelong medical learners enrolled across its distribution network, as well as to third-party medical schools. In addition, it offers printed and digital content, as well as an online medical education platform and physicians, healthcare professionals and students. Afya Limited was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Belo Horizonte, Brazil.

financial_summary: Afya Limited is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $929M market cap on $672M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 10% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 63% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $248M in free cash flow — roughly 37 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.99× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.2% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 79% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 26pp above the Consumer Defensive median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 4.07x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+20.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.07 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 38% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 35% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 43% and a beta of 0.86, it moves roughly with the market.
About $2.9M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 3.2x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 54% in the 2020 crash and 43% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 81% below its DCF fair value of $54.72, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 34%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $43.52 to $69.36 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Defensive peers: P/E 6.4 vs 18.5, EV/EBITDA 2.0 vs 10.3 and P/FCF 3.7 vs 16.0 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 65% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 26.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $15.87 on average, 51% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 10.0% by 7pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.11).
It runs a 63% gross margin and converts 37% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 1.99x, but high accruals (-8.2% of assets).
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.6x net debt to EBITDA ($204.5M of cash against $373.3M of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.2x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 13.6% over 3 years and 23.0% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 13%).
At current returns, reinvesting 47% of profits supports about 8.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 34.7% a year over five years.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.8% on average.
Analysts expect 7.4% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 78.5%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 20%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $2.5M sold).
It returns 2.9% a year to shareholders (6.3% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 47.1% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 9,395 employees, each generates about $72K of revenue, 0.1x the Consumer Defensive median, and productivity has risen 23.1% a year.
That works out to $26K of free cash flow per employee.
